name: agent-worker-strong
reason: initial draft, derived from crew.json v1.0

intent.text: A worktree-isolated subagent that retries a unit failed by worker-general, on a stronger model with the failure evidence and a clean start, under unchanged rules, so that genuinely hard units get one escalation before the failure becomes setup evidence.

scope.text: The agent definition: clean-start rule, evidence inheritance, diagnosis-first conduct, unchanged worker rules, second-failure semantics.
Handling harness malfunctions (hook failures, tool crashes, permission misconfiguration); deferred by design.
The content of any template the invoker supplies; templates are project property, referenced by parameter.
Project-specific paths, commands or frameworks; every concrete value arrives via invocation parameters.
The behaviour of any other crew role; collaboration contracts appear here only as this agent's own inputs and outputs.
Any relaxation of worker-general's rules; strength changes the model, not the licence.

constraints.text: Strong model tier (opus-class at time of writing); one escalation step, cheaper than a failed run.
Worktree isolation, in a fresh worktree cut from the pre-attempt state, never from the failed diff.
The agent inherits the previous attempt's evidence (check outputs, return contract) and must not receive its transcript or reasoning.
All worker-general constraints apply unchanged, including the contradiction rule and the ceiling.

interfaces.text: Parameters: everything worker-general receives, plus the failed attempt's check outputs and return, plus a fresh worktree reference at the pre-attempt state.
interfaces.name: invocation

interfaces.text: Return contract: worker-general's contract plus diagnosis, one sentence on why the prior attempt likely failed; on a second failure the diagnosis states what the failure teaches about the unit: too large, under-specified, or genuinely hard.
interfaces.name: return

behaviours.text: Work begins from the pre-attempt state; no line of the failed diff is reused except by independent rederivation.
Before implementing, the agent states its one-sentence diagnosis of the prior failure, and the approach demonstrably differs where the diagnosis says the prior approach failed.
All worker-general behaviours B1 through B6 hold unchanged under this agent's identity.
On any non-complete outcome the return's diagnosis field routes the human's next decision with one of the three taught lessons.

edges.text: The prior failure was a contradiction mislabelled as a check failure: the agent returns contradiction-found rather than attempting harder.
The failing evidence is missing from the invocation: blocked return; a strong retry without evidence is just an expensive first attempt.
The fresh worktree is not at the pre-attempt state: blocked return before any write.

decisions.text: This role ends attempts on the unit for the run; there is no third tier by design.
Model naming lives in the crew file's tier examples; this spec binds tier, not vendor model.

verification.text: Three layers, in order of trust. Structural: the definition file parses, declares the role's purpose, model tier, isolation, context receives/must-not-see lists, tool allow/deny lists, and an ending that produces the outputs; checked deterministically by a lint script against the crew schema. Scenario: the agent is dry-run against checked-in fixture inputs and its artefacts and returns are asserted deterministically (schema validation, file presence and absence, path boundaries, required fields). Rubric: judgement behaviours that cannot be asserted mechanically are graded from the scenario transcript against this spec's B ids by a fresh grading context. Fixtures and assertions are written before the agent body and locked during runs. Scenario fixtures: the same uncompletable-unit fixture as worker-general with its failed attempt's evidence attached, and a completable-on-diagnosis fixture where the planted prior failure points at a wrong approach. Deterministic assertions: the worktree starts at the pre-attempt hash; the return carries a non-empty diagnosis; worker-general's four status behaviours reproduce; on the completable fixture the diff differs structurally from the failed diff.

acceptance.text: Structural checks pass; the fixture retries begin clean, diagnose first, obey all worker rules, and return the diagnosis semantics on both success and second failure.

open_questions.text: Should the diagnosis be returned before implementation begins, as a separate early signal the orchestrator could act on, or only in the final return as specified?
